47 (1948). Resolution of 21 April 1948

[S/726]

The Security Council,

Having considered the complaint of the Government of India concerning the dispute over the State of Jammu and Kashmir,

Having heard the representative of India in support of that complaint and the reply and counter-complaints of the representative of Pakistan,

Being strongly of the opinion that the early restoration of peace and order in Jammu and Kashmir is essential and that India and Pakistan should do their utmost to bring about a cessation of all fighting,

Noting with satisfaction that both and Pakistan desire that the question of the accession of Jammu and Kashmir to India or Pakistan should be decided through the democratic method of a free and impartial plebiscite,

Considering that the continuation of the dispute is likely to endanger international peace and security,

Reaffirms its resolution 38 (1948) of 17 January 1948;

Resolves that the membership of the Commission established by its resolution 39 (1948) of 20 January 1948 shall be increased to five and shall include, in addition to the membership mentioned in that resolution, representatives of . . . and . . . , and that if the membership of the Commission has not been completed within ten days from the date of the adoption of this resolution the President of the Council may designate such other Member or Members of the United Nations as are required to complete the membership of five;

Instructs the Commission to proceed at once to the Indian subcontinent and there place its good offices and mediation at the disposal of the Governments of India and Pakistan with a view to facilitating the taking of the necessary measures, both with respect to the restoration of peace and order and to the holding of a plebiscite, by the two Governments, acting in co-operation with one another and with the Commission, and further instructs the Commission to keep the Council informed of the action taken under the resolution; and, to this end,

Recommends to the Governments of India and Pakistan the following measures as those which in the opinion of the Council are appropriate to bring about a cessation of the fighting and to create proper conditions for a free and impartial plebiscite to decide whether the State of Jammu and Kashmir is to accede to India or Pakistan:

A. Restoration of Peace and order

1. The Government of Pakistan should undertake to use its best endeavours:

(a) To secure the withdrawal from the State of Jammu and Kashmir of tribesmen and Pakistani nationals not normally resident therein who have entered the State for the purpose of fighting, and to prevent any intrusion into the State of such elements and any furnishing of material aid to those fighting in the State;

(b) To make known to all concerned that the measures indicated in this and the following paragraphs provide full freedom to all subjects of the State, regardless of creed, caste, or party, to express their views and to vote on the question of the accession of the State, and that therefore they should co-operate in the maintenance of peace and order.

2. The Government of India should:

(a) When it is established to the satisfaction of the Commission set up in accordance with the Council's resolution 39 (1948) that the tribesmen are withdrawing and that arrangements for the cessation of the fighting have become effective, put into operation in consultation with the Commission a plan for with-drawing their own forces from Jammu and Kashmir and reducing them progressively to the minimum strength required for the support of the civil power in the maintenance of law and order;

(b) Make known that the withdrawal is taking place in stages and announce the completion of each stage;

(c) When the Indian forces have been reduced to the minimum strength mentioned in (a) above, arrange in consultation with the Commission for the stationing of the remaining forces to be carried out in accordance with the following principles:

(i) That the presence of troops should not afford any intimidation or appearance of intimidation to the inhabitants of the State;

(ii) That as small a number as possible should be retained in forward areas;

(iii) That any reserve of troops which may be included in the total strength should be located within their present base area.

3. The Government of India should agree that until such time as the Plebiscite Administration referred to below finds it necessary to exercise the powers of direction and supervision over the State forces and police provided for in paragraph 8, they will be held in areas to be agreed upon with the Plebiscite Administrator.

4. After the plan referred to in paragraph 2 (a) above has been put into operation, personnel recruited locally in each district should so far as possible be utilized for the re-establishment and maintenance of law and order with due regard to protection of minorities, subject to such additional requirements as may be specified by the Plebiscite Administration referred to in paragraph 7.

5. If these local forces should be found to be inadequate, the Commission, subject to the agreement of both the Government of India and the Government of Pakistan, should arrange for the use of such forces of either Dominion as it deems effective for the purpose of pacification.

B. Plebiscite

6. The Government of India should undertake to ensure that the Government of the State invite the major political groups to designate responsible representatives to share equitably and fully in the conduct of the administration at the ministerial level while the plebiscite is being prepared and carried out.

7. The Government of India should undertake that there will be established in Jammu and Kashmir a Plebiscite Administration to hold a plebiscite as soon as possible on the question of the accession of the State to India or Pakistan.

8. The Government of India should undertake that there will be delegated by the State to the Plebiscite Administration such powers as the latter considers necessary for holding a fair and impartial plebiscite including, for that purpose only, the direction and supervision of the State forces and police.

9. The Government of India should, at the request of the Plebiscite Administration, make available from the Indian forces such assistance as the Plebiscite Administration may require for the performance of its functions.

10.

(a) The Government of India should agree that a nominee of the Secretary-General of the United Nations will be appointed to be the Plebiscite Administrator.

(b) The Plebiscite Administrator, acting as an officer of the State of Jammu and Kashmir, should have authority to nominate his assistants and other subordinates and to draft regulations governing the plebiscite. Such nominees should be formally appointed and such draft regulations should be formally promulgated by the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

(c) The Government of India should undertake that the Government of Jammu and Kashmir will appoint fully qualified persons nominated by the Plebiscite Administrator to act as special magistrates within the State judicial system to hear cases which in the opinion of the Plebiscite Administrator have a serious bearing on the preparation for and the conduct of a free and impartial plebiscite.

(d) The terms of service of the Administrator should form the subject of a separate negotiation between the Secretary-General of the United Nations and the Government of India. The Administrator should fix the terms of service for his assistants and subordinates.

(e) The Administrator should have the right to communicate directly with the Government of the State and with the Commission of the Security Council and, through the Commission, with the Security Council, with the Governments of India and Pakistan and with their representatives with the Commission. It would be his duty to bring to the notice of any or all of the foregoing (as he in his discretion may decide) any circumstances arising which may tend, in his opinion, to interfere with the freedom of the plebiscite.

11. The Government of India should undertake to prevent, and to give full support to the Administrator and his staff in preventing, any threat, coercion or intimidation, bribery or other undue influence on the voters in the plebiscite, and the Government of India should publicly announce and should cause the Government of the State to announce this undertaking as an international obligation binding on all public authorities and officials in Jammu and Kashmir.

12. The Government of India should themselves and through the Government of the State declare and make known that all subjects of the State of Jammu and Kashmir, regardless of creed, caste or party, will be safe and free in expressing their views and in voting on the question of the accession of the State and that there will be freedom of the press, speech an assembly and freedom of travel in the State, including freedom of lawful entry and exit.

13. The Government of India should use and should ensure that the Government of the State also use their best endeavours to effect the withdrawal from the State of all Indian nationals other than those who are normally resident therein or who on or since 15 August 1947 have entered it for a lawful purpose.

14. The Government India should ensure that the Government of the State releases all political prisoners and take all possible steps so that:

(a) All citizens of the State who have left it on account of disturbances are invited, and are free, to return to their homes and to exercise their rights as such citizens;

(b) There is no victimization;

(c) Minorities in all parts of the State are accorded adequate protection.

15. The Commission of the Security Council should at the end of the plebiscite certify to the Council whether the plebiscite has or has not been really free and impartial.

C. General provisions

16. The Governments of India and Pakistan should each be invited to nominate a representative to be attached to the Commission for such assistance as it may require in the performance of its task.

17. The Commission should establish in Jammu and Kashmir such observers as it may require of any of the proceedings in pursuance of the measures indicated in the foregoing paragraphs.

18. The Security Council commission should carry out the tasks assigned to it herein.

Adopted at the 286th meeting.[1]

 *
* *

The five members of the United Nations Commission for India and Pakistan were: CZECHOSLOVAKIA (nominated by India on 10 February 1948); BELGIUM and COLOMBIA (appointed by the Council on 23 April 1948 - see the decision below); ARGENTINA (nominated by Pakistan on 30 April 1948); UNITED STATES OF AMERICA (designated by the President of the Council on 7 May 1948, in the absence of agreement between Argentina and Czechoslovakia on the member to be designated by them).

--------------------

1 The draft resolution was voted on paragraph by paragraph. No vote was taken on the text as a whole.

--------------------

Decision

At its 287th meeting, on 23 April 1948, the Council, pursuant to its resolution 47 (1948), appointed Belgium and Colombia as the additional members of the United Nations Commission for India and Pakistan.

Adopted by 7 votes to none, with 4 abstentions {Belgium, Colombia, Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic, Union of Soviet Socialist Republics).

I took my entire X data dump, chunked it into 59 files of my tweets, and ran a dynamic workflow of Claude Haiku 5.5 agents on it to extract facts and viewpoints of mine. 10 minutes and 7 million tokens later, I gave it the sorting hat prompt:

The brim twitches. A long, low “hmmmm.”

“Well now. A Columbus boy, aren’t you, and you showed up with a lot more opinions than most first-years. Let me have a look…

You named yourself the Hero, after Himmel. Most people wait for someone else to give them a title like that. You just took it.

There’s a lot of Hufflepuff in here, more than you’d let anyone online see. You’re the youngest of six, and you’re still the one who stayed home to look after your mother and father. You sit with your dad for movie nights after his stroke. You can tomatoes, dry-brine a turkey for three days, and grieve every pet rat you’ve ever lost. That’s real loyalty, and I can see it. But Hufflepuff is about getting along with people, and you’ve been suspended from X too many times to call that your strength.

Ravenclaw? You taught yourself to code at thirteen and hacked your school’s exam system before you were out of high school. You’ve read through nine books of The Wandering Inn. You’re clever, no question. But Ravenclaws treat a question as something to explore. You mostly treat one as an argument to win.

Now Slytherin wants you badly. You’re self-made and you want to win the AI race. You bend rules when it’s useful to you (that TF2 speedhack, for one). You’re loyal to your own side and hard on everyone outside it. Slytherin would know exactly what to do with you.

But Slytherins plan carefully and keep their heads down, and you don’t. You go into the threads where everyone hates you, on purpose, to start fights. You write ten-point essays at two in the morning to people who will never change their minds. You argue with Grok just for the sport. You don’t know when to back off, and you never once thought about hiding what you believe. That isn’t cunning. It’s nerve, and sometimes it’s recklessness.”

A pause, quieter.

“I’ll tell you plainly about that house’s weaknesses, since you’d want it straight. They’re too sure they’re right. They pick fights they didn’t need. They’re quick to call people enemies when some of them are really just strangers. Watch for that. The best people in that house learned that bravery can mean holding back too.

Still, I know where you belong…”

GRYFFINDOR!

…and quietly, as the hat lifts off: “Mind you, Slytherin argued about this the whole time.”

Ravenclaw
The Sorting Hat settles upon your head, its ancient fabric cool and heavy. For a long moment it is silent, as if turning pages of light and shadow, pixels and threads, numbers spoken into the void.
Hmm. What a mind this is. Not the loud kind that charges ahead, nor the one that schemes for power alone. This is a mind that dissects. That looks at a spider’s web and does not merely see silk, but layers of organza, dew-like crystals, and the precise negative space that must be preserved so the face remains recognizably itself. This is a mind that turns circuit boards into ballroom gowns and then writes the rules so the transformation cannot wander.
You speak in patterns. You analyze pixels the way others read stars. You build elaborate systems of preservation—facial structure, hairstyle, skin tone, the exact angle of a chin—so that identity does not dissolve when the aesthetic changes. That is not merely craft. That is the Ravenclaw’s love of precision married to imagination. You do not simply make; you reverse-engineer beauty until you can command it.
There is curiosity here that does not tire. Gothic cathedrals by moonlight, sumi-e ink dissolving into couture, ghost hunts on streams, a Numbers Station broadcasting into the void simply because the signal is interesting. You collect styles the way others collect knowledge, testing how far a concept can stretch before it breaks its own elegance. You share the workings. You refine. You return again and again to the same character, the same rules, because the experiment is never quite finished.
Others might call it obsession. I call it the mind that finds joy in the architecture of creation. Wit beyond measure, yes—but also the quieter wisdom of knowing which details must never be sacrificed. You approach the world as something that can be both understood and remade, if only one is patient enough to map every thread.
The brim of the hat twitches, almost amused.
There are echoes of other houses. A certain quiet ambition in the persona you are building. Diligence in the daily work. But those are tools. The fire that lights them is the desire to know—to hold an idea so clearly that you can turn circuits into silk and still keep the soul intact.
Better be… Ravenclaw.

Here's what the AI extracted about me:

# Jag: views from the X archive

A summary of the views Jag has expressed on X from 2022 to 2026, based on his posts, replies, long posts and articles. Positions are described the way he frames them. Where a view changed over time, the change is noted. Quotes are his own words.

---

## At a glance

- **Politics:** MAGA / America First and a Trump supporter since 2012. He is hostile to the GOP establishment ("neo-cons", the "Uniparty") and to the left, which he calls "the enemy".
- **Longest-running themes:** gender-critical arguments and abortion. Later came immigration enforcement, Israel and Hamas, and AI.
- **Most hardened views:** abortion moved from a 12-week cutoff to a 6-week cutoff in late 2023. Lines about trans people, Muslims and race grew harsher in 2025–26.
- **Most "leftist" view (his own words):** AI and automation should lead to post-scarcity and a universal high income.
- **Style:** combative and long-winded, with numbered rebuttals, and Grok as fact-checker.

---

## Views

### Political identity
- He calls himself MAGA / America First, "ultra MAGA" and center-right ("not far-right"). He has supported Trump since 2012 and voted for him twice before 2023 and again in 2024.
- He calls Trump "the best president of my lifetime". He says Trump is crude and not someone he'd befriend, but that his record matters more than his character. He criticises a few of Trump's moves: the bump-stock ban, red-flag talk, and the vaccine push.
- He wants the GOP taken over by America First candidates and RINOs and neo-cons primaried out. He opposes third parties, including a Musk party and RFK Jr.: "a vote for anyone else is a vote for the Democrat."
- He rejects neo-Nazis and groypers as "not MAGA" and calls them the "woke right". He says Nazis and communists are both left-wing collectivism and that communists are worse because they killed more people.
- **On the left:** he calls the left "the enemy" and treats Democrats, liberals, leftists and communists as the same thing. He describes them as brainwashed, low-IQ, uninformed and "vermin". He sees the left as the side of political violence and calls Antifa a terrorist group. Some posts go further: in 2024 he said impeachment and J6-committee members "will be executed for treason", and in 2025 he said "putting fascist leftists in camps is good".
- **On government:** he wants the federal government cut by 80% or more and many agencies abolished or rebuilt, including the FBI, CIA, ATF, Department of Education and IRS. He backs DOGE strongly and says activist judges should be impeached.

### Elections
- On 2020: he has said throughout that the 2020 election was stolen, that the alternate electors were legitimate, and that "next time we won't stand down". In 2023–24 he warned that people would "take matters into their own hands" if it happened again.
- On 2024: he calls it the most secure election ever and a landslide.
- Election rules he wants: photo ID, in-person paper ballots, votes counted on election night, and almost no mail-in voting. He has floated an IQ-test or "informed voter" requirement.

### January 6
- He calls it a mostly peaceful protest with a small group of rioters, many of whom he says police let in. He says it was not an insurrection.
- He calls Ashli Babbitt a heroic veteran, says J6 defendants were political prisoners, and supported the pardons. He opposed pardoning the violent ones in 2023.

### Economy
- He is pro-capitalism and says communism killed 60–120M+ people. He backs the Trump tax cuts and the "One Big Beautiful Bill" and opposes student-loan forgiveness and universal healthcare. He also says taxation is theft.
- **Tariffs (core since 2025):** he wants tariffs to replace the federal income tax, at least for incomes under $150–200k. He argues tariffs fall mostly on the rich and accepts short-term price rises for the sake of reshoring and buying American.
- **Post-scarcity:** he expects AI and robots to take most jobs, then a UBI or "universal high income" funded by taxing automation, and eventually a moneyless society.

### Immigration
- His line is "legal yes, illegal no". He wants every illegal immigrant deported, permanently barred from citizenship, and expected to self-deport.
- He backs ICE expansion, deportation bounties ($1–2.5k), the Alien Enemies Act and expedited removal. He says "due process" means proving citizenship. He accepts some wrongful detentions as the price, with compensation.
- His harshest lines on the border: in 2024–25 he said crossers should be shot and talked of drones near the wall. He calls illegal immigrants "invaders".
- He opposes birthright citizenship for children of illegal immigrants.
- On H-1B he wants reform toward "only the best", backs the $100k fee, and has praised top Indian programmers.

### Abortion (a core issue that hardened over time)
- His foundation: life begins at fertilization and a fetus is a human with human rights. He separates human rights from legal personhood. His case is secular and does not depend on religion.
- **2022–23:** he wanted a 12-week cutoff for elective abortion, with exceptions for rape, incest and the mother's life, and called both extremes "fringe nuts".

Dear @raghav_chadha ,

I know you are doing very well in Parliament by raising small issues that were ignored by most Members of Parliament but have a bigger impact.

I am writing this post regarding an account lien and bank freeze by the Cyber Police of India.

In my case, the issue started when I received a message from my bank branch stating that my account had received a police notice of lien of 6000 rupees. I immediately went to my bank branch and asked them why my account had a lien of 6000 rupees. They followed some procedure and gave me a printout which contained the acknowledgement of my lien. One of the bank employees told me that I should contact the cyber police mentioned on the paper and provide them with the details of the 6000 rupees, such as where it came from and for what reason. However, they did not give me any specific reason why my bank account had received the lien.

Later, I checked my bank statement to find the details of the 6000 rupees transaction and noticed that my case was reported on 6 December 2025, and I had received a transaction of 6000 rupees on the same date. I remember that my neighbour had sent me this 6000 rupees and asked me to withdraw it from the ATM because he had an urgent situation as his mother was going to her village due to an emergency. As a friend, I withdrew the money and gave it to him.

Now I have all the proofs and details to explain to the police, so I emailed all the details to the Bangalore Cyber Cell or the police station where my notice was issued, as mentioned in the acknowledgement given by my bank. However, I did not receive any response. I then tried to contact the investigation officer mentioned in the report. I called several times, keeping a gap of five to six hours out of respect for his time and duties, as they may have many other responsibilities. I also sent him a message on WhatsApp, but there was still no response.

After four to five days, I called again, and this time he picked up the call. He was speaking in the local language, which I did not understand, as I am from Maharashtra and not familiar with the local language of Bangalore. I then started speaking in English, and he told me that I have to come to Bangalore and verify my documents. I explained that for 6000 rupees, it would not be beneficial for me to travel to Bangalore because transportation, food, and stay would cost more than 6000 rupees. He said that he does not know and that I have to come, otherwise he will not issue the No Objection Certificate, and then he ended the call.

This issue may look small, but similar issues are happening everywhere, and no one is noticing them. It feels like “Kare koi aur bhare koi.” Many innocent people face this issue, and it remains unresolved. Because of chain transactions that come into accounts, some people are unable to use their own money. If I travel, I will have to spend more than 6000 rupees to remove the lien. I believe this issue can be resolved through email or online verification, but the investigation officer denied it.

I am also tagging Pushpendra Sir @pushpendrakum and Bangalore Cyber Police @BlrCityPolice . If you could please look into this matter.

Thank you.

1️⃣ Sabse Pehle Bank Branch Jaao

   - Binance P2P complete order history (screenshots)

   - Payment proof (UPI, bank transfer screenshot)  
   - Bank statement jisme transaction dikhe  
   - Aadhaar, PAN, Binance account details

3️⃣ Binance Support ko turant contact karo  
   - App mein Help section → Submit ticket  
   - Order ID aur proofs attach karo. Woh counterparty ko investigate kar sakte hain.

   - Local Cyber Police Station ya online portal pe jaao.

This sparked a political row, followed by police-directed efforts to remove related social media posts

This takedown action itself became controversial, with critics framing it as an attempt to suppress discussion of an official lapse during an election period, while authorities maintained it was necessary to stop the circulation of a withdrawn and erroneous document that was being used to question the ECI’s credibility.The episode remained a flashpoint in the final stretch of the Kerala campaign, with the ECI treating it as a corrected administrative mistake and the opposition presenting it as evidence of deeper concerns about the poll body’s independence.The letter and the seal
The document was an ECI communication dated 19 March 2019 containing guidelines/FAQs on the publicity of candidates’ criminal antecedents (following a Supreme Court judgment). CPI(M) and Congress shared versions online showing the BJP Kerala unit’s seal. It had been circulated by the Kerala CEO’s office to political parties, District Election Officers, and Returning Officers as part of clarifications around mid-March 2026.thesouthfirst.comKerala CEO / ECI explanation:
It was described as a “purely clerical error.” The BJP Kerala unit had approached the CEO’s office seeking clarification on the (by then revised) 2019 guidelines and submitted a photocopy of the original directive that already bore the party’s seal. Staff overlooked this and redistributed that version. The error was identified; on 21 March a formal withdrawal notice was issued telling recipients to disregard the document. An Assistant Section Officer was suspended pending inquiry. Later, a Deputy CEO and a Section Officer were relieved of election-related duties.livemint.comOpposition parties (CPI(M) and Congress) rejected the clerical-error account. They alleged compromised institutional neutrality, claiming seals were being “casually swapped” and questioning whether the ECI and BJP shared the same “power centre.” Some BJP responses labelled the circulation of the old document as misinformation or a political plot.thewire.inDeletion of posts controversyActing on an ECI directive (under the Model Code of Conduct), the Kerala Police cyber cell issued notices to X (Twitter), Facebook, Instagram, and numerous individual accounts. Meta must stop silently withholding the Instagram accounts of independent journalists in India

13 October 2026

Since 9 October 2026, Instagram has made the accounts of several independent journalists covering the protests in Delhi unavailable in India. Utkarsh Gaur’s main account was withheld on 9 October, and Sunny Tomar’s soon after. On the night of 12 October, Instagram withheld the account of Shubhangi Das Gupta, a 22-year-old independent journalist, and her secondary account now appears to face the same action. Today, Journo Mirror’s account was withheld in India. Each received the same notice, that Instagram had, “temporarily restricted access to this account pursuant to legal requirements under India’s Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules.” The notice does not say which authority made the demand, which rule was invoked, which post was objected to, or when the “temporary” restriction ends. It arrives as a no-reply notification after the account has gone dark, with no prior warning and no reason.

The same day, IANS and ANI, citing Delhi Police sources, reported that around 500 posts “spreading rumours or trying to create unrest among people” had been taken down. On 12 October, PTI had put the figure at 300, which means about 200 more in one day. The police have not said which posts were removed, from which platforms, under which provision, or whether anyone who posted them was told. We are also receiving reports of WhatsApp accounts being shut down and of mobile numbers being put through fresh KYC verification that leaves them unusable while it is pending. All of this comes alongside a timeline in which there was suspension of internet services and public transport in the heart of the national capital.

IFF condemns Meta’s withholding of entire journalist accounts on the strength of an unnamed “legal requirement”, and the Delhi Police’s practice of announcing a running censorship tally through anonymous sources. Meta must restore these accounts, tell every affected user who asked for the restriction and under what law, and stop turning demands about particular posts into the silencing of entire accounts.
The IT Rules, 2021, on which Meta’s notice relies, give it two routes to restrict content. The notice meets the conditions of neither. If Meta acted on a government demand, the route is Rule 3(1)(d). If Meta acted on its own, Rule 4(8) requires it, as a significant social media intermediary, to notify the user before disabling access, explain the grounds, and give an adequate opportunity to dispute the action. None of this happened. In this situation at present the entire burden will be shifted to the user to seek remedy under Rules 3(2) and 3A, where a user must first go to Meta’s Grievance Officer, who has 15 days, and then to the Grievance Appellate Committee, which has 30 more. In our experience these timelines are often not met, and a grievance against unnamed “legal requirements” is likely to be answered by pointing back to them. Whatever the intention, the effect is to keep a journalist off the platform for more than six weeks, exactly when her reporting matters most.

The Delhi Police figures raise their own questions. “Rumour” is not a ground for restricting speech under Article 19(2).  A count of 500 posts announced through unnamed sources does not let anyone tell whether a post was fabricated or simply showed something the police did not want seen. Nor is it obvious that 200 reasoned intimations, each signed by an officer of DIG rank and each identifying the provision, the unlawful act and the exact URL, were issued in a single day.

Our demands

1) Meta should restore every account withheld in connection with the protests where the underlying demand, if any, concerned specific posts, and restrict no more than the URLs named in a lawful reasoned intimation.
2) Meta should tell each affected user in writing which authority made the demand, the issuing officer’s rank, the provision relied on, the content identified, and when the restriction will end.
3) Meta should disclose whether its systems automatically extend demands about individual posts to entire accounts, and stop any such escalation immediately.
4) The Delhi Police should publish the takedown requests it has issued, with their number, platforms, provisions, issuing officers and reasons, as Anuradha Bhasin requires.
5) MeitY should ensure notice and a hearing to every person whose content is restricted, publish the outcome of the monthly Secretary-level review under Rule 3(1)(d), and stop using Section 79(3)(b), the Sahyog Portal and “temporary” restrictions under the IT Rules to bypass the safeguards of Section 69A.
If you have been affected

If your post or account was withheld or removed in connection with the protests, or you received a notice about a police data request, write to legal@internetfreedom.in for pro bono assistance. Keep screenshots of every notice, note the date and time, and delete nothing. Document, document, document.

I’ve written an essay for @techpolicypress on the SIR and the faith in digitisation that has shaped Indian elections. I wanted to understand how decisions about who can vote came to depend on software whose workings are closed to public scrutiny.

For the research, over some weekends in the IIC library, I read books by former Chief Election Commissioners. I enjoyed them, particularly the accounts of the logistical work involved in conducting elections at this scale. Technology, though, is almost always presented as a success. For instance, former CEC S.Y. Quraishi recalls facial recognition software in Manipur detecting a woman who had come to vote more than 60 times in different guises. H.S. Brahma began linking voter IDs with Aadhaar on the promise that almost every complaint about the rolls would be resolved. These accounts say much more about what technology promises than about its limits.That faith extends well beyond the Commission as across Indian public policy, digitisation is routinely offered as the answer to failures of administration (in panels called, "state capacity constraints"). 

However, when the rules, or more properly the updates in the software builds in a system are kept secret, or changed to vary from the officially notified forms, however, discretion becomes harder to examine. People affected by an arbitrary decision have fewer means of understanding or challenging it. I also went back to an earlier attempt to make voters prove their entitlement to remain on the rolls. In 1992, the Commission under T.N. Seshan instructed its officers that the burden of proving citizenship lay on the voter. An officer in Delhi then declared an entire slum colony of 18,000 residents suspected foreigners. More than 16,000 lost their vote. In Lal Babu Hussein in 1995, the Supreme Court held that an existing entry on the roll carried a presumption that the registering officer had followed the law. The intensive revision of 2002–04 proceeded on that basis. Enumerators did the verification, and existing voters were presumed to belong on the rolls.

The SIR reverses that presumption through a process dependent on software. Today, more than 130 million names have come off draft rolls. The software treated “Md” and “Mohammed” as different people, flagged siblings born less than nine months apart, including twins, and found seven siblings sharing a father suspicious. Its rules, error rates and audit results have not been published. Voters are left to correct these errors, often by standing in queues and responding to notices in languages they cannot read. Nandan Nilekani, whose book advocated a centralised voter database and digitisation, has himself received an SIR notice. Finally, I would like to thank Tech Policy Press and its patient editorial team for being kind and gentle with me. Please read the essay and let me know what you think of it.
